The machine is 17 % busy on 8 cores: one thread is the limit. The cost grows with the memory of the server: on the morning of 13 Nov, at 2.3 GiB and 15 ssh per second, the server saturated with about 10 remote runs (STUDIO-0020 lowered the count of starts, not the cost of one start).

patches.title: A monitor whose last allowed check was triggered, or whose timeout passed, without a next check wakes its owner once
patches.problem: Production, studio.17, 14 Nov 2026, TR-915 (Game Integrator): an external-service monitor (TeamCity Debug, maxAttempts 3, timeoutAt 23:31:41Z, recoveryPolicy escalate_to_board) ran its third check at 23:01:37 and then ended silently: no next check, state triggered 3/3, no comment, no activity, no wake. The limit handling (heartbeat/scheduling.ts, issueMonitorLimitClearReason and clearIssueMonitorAndRecover) runs only when a scheduled check falls due with nextAttemptCount above maxAttempts, while rescheduling is refused once attemptCount reaches maxAttempts ('Monitor bounds are already exhausted', issue-execution-policy.ts); the timeout acts only on a scheduled check too. So the attempt limit was unreachable and every recovery policy dead after the last check. Three roles (Game Integrator, CEO on TR-978, Infra Manager on TR-969) then searched for an automatic Board escalation and asked the owner for a way to reach Paperclip support.

A run scheduled for retry, queued or running (linked by issue_id), a pending question and a pending approval linked to the task each leave the monitor triggered with no wake or comment, and the first tick after it clears settles it. A reassigned task (the last check went to another agent) and a trigger older than 24 h wake nobody. nextIssueMonitorAt returns the timeout of a triggered monitor that has no next check. patches.migration: None. The monitor tick also looks, once a minute at most, at every visible open task (in_progress or in_review, assigned to an agent only) whose monitor is triggered with no next check and no monitor left in the policy, and either attemptCount >= maxAttempts with the last trigger less than 24 h old, or a timeoutAt passed less than 24 h ago, provided the current assignee received the last check (a wake keyed issue-monitor:<task>:... within ten minutes before the trigger). It acts only while nothing is running or waiting on the task: no run queued, running or scheduled for retry (by issue_id, native issue, issueId or taskId), no execution or checkout run, no held wake (deferred_issue_execution), no open recovery action, no pending question, no pending approval linked to the task, and no review stage waiting on a person. It wakes the assignee first (issue_monitor_recovery, idempotency key issue-monitor-recovery:<task>:<clearReason>:<lastTriggeredAt>; a wake already admitted under that key is reused); with create_recovery_issue it creates or reuses the child recovery task instead. Only once that follow-up is admitted does it, in one transaction, clear the monitor state (max_attempts_exhausted or timeout_exceeded), post a comment saying what to do and that there is no Paperclip support (ask the Board with a question on the task), and log issue.monitor_exhausted, issue.monitor_escalated_to_board for that policy and issue.monitor_recovery_wake_queued. If the wake cannot be admitted (paused or non-invokable agent, blocked budget, execution hold, task changed), nothing is cleared: issue.monitor_deferred is logged at most once an hour and the next tick tries again with the same key. Once per exhausted monitor: the cleared state is no longer a candidate, so a role that re-arms nothing is not woken again. nextIssueMonitorAt also returns a time for such candidates and the timeout of a triggered monitor that has no next check. Deliberate policy difference: with escalate_to_board, the scheduled path (a due check past its bounds) only comments, while this catch-up also wakes the owner, so a monitor never ends without its owner being told. Known cost: the candidate scan reads issues by JSONB fields without a dedicated index, at most once a minute while a candidate waits. Past 24 h without an admitted wake (up to 7 days), the monitor is ended once with a comment saying its owner could not be woken and why, and issue.monitor_exhausted (wake not_admitted); older states are left alone. A held wake is retried at most every 15 minutes per task. Before installing, count the tasks in this state in production (read-only query kept in the studio workspace review notes). Known limit (bench, lot 19, 15 Nov 2026): when the agent is paused, the existing pause handling opens a stranded_assigned_issue action and blocks the task (Board card); this catch-up only looks at in_progress or in_review tasks, so it does not act then. On resume the existing issue_wakes_missed_during_pause wake starts the role, and a disposition repair (deliberate_wait_without_target) may follow and keep the catch-up away (open recovery action): the role is woken and the Board was told, but without this patch's 'what to do' comment; the monitor stays triggered until the 24 h exit writes its note, provided the task is back in_progress or in_review within 7 days. No case found where neither the role nor the Board is told.

patches.title: An ssh lease probe that cannot connect is a transient environment failure, retried with the existing budget
patches.problem: Production, 15 Nov 2026, TR-999: the Feedback Manager's assignment run (server ssh environment QA-C) failed in 12 s with setup_failed, 'Failed to acquire lease for environment "QA-C" (ssh)', ssh stderr 'ssh: connect to host 100.121.114.90 port 22: Connection timed out', before any provider work; the stranded-task recovery blocked the task one second later. The bounded retry of transient lease failures (environment_provider_unavailable) only reads structured evidence (HTTP status or a network errno); ssh exits 255 with no code, so a briefly unreachable machine was a permanent setup failure.

patches.migration: None. runSshCommand (used by ensureSshWorkspaceReady, the ssh lease probe) attaches, to an ssh failure with exit 255, an empty stdout (nothing ran remotely, so a remote command that already started is never retried) and a stderr line says the connection never happened, a cause with the matching network code (connect timed out / operation timed out / banner exchange timed out -> ETIMEDOUT; connection refused -> ECONNREFUSED; no route to host / network unreachable -> ENETUNREACH). The existing classifier (readTransientEnvironmentProviderFailure, which walks causes) then makes it environment_provider_unavailable, retried with the bounded bootstrap budget and, if still failing, blocked with the 'provider temporarily unavailable, no agent work started' card. Authentication, host key and name resolution failures are unchanged (not retried). The error message itself is unchanged. The ssh environment is left unchanged (no forced locale): the default client config of the Paperclip server sends LANG and LC_* (/etc/ssh/ssh_config, SendEnv LANG LC_*) and macOS machines accept them, so a forced LC_ALL would reach the remote command; OpenSSH sets only LC_CTYPE itself, and the server has only the C, C.utf8, POSIX and en_US.utf8 locales, so the connection diagnostics stay in English. The retry budget is unchanged (2 attempts, 30 s then 60 s): a machine asleep longer ends on the 'provider unavailable, no work started' card, and waking it is an infrastructure matter.

Cold review, defects found in v6 and fixed: (P1) a hand-back run on "only cancelled blockers left" is bounded and never qualified, so the backstop woke every 30 s without end, as it did while a router refused: a run now qualifies through its admission's hand-over mark, the wait between two backstop wakes doubles up to 1 h, and an issue with an active recovery action is left to its owner; (P2) the base was the run's start although the batch is computed at admission: it is now the admission time; (P3) a repeated automatic hold only moves updatedAt of the earlier request, and a run cancelled at the claim gate was dated at its creation: the trace reads requestedAt, updatedAt, finishedAt and the cancellation time; (P4) after a reassignment written by a service, without activity, the new assignee had no trace: while it has no base, a hold of any agent counts; (P5) a ready wake merged into a bounded run already running removed its mark and gave it a batch it never showed: the merge changes neither once the run started; (P6) one failing wake stopped the wakes of the following dependents: one send per dependent, each logged; (P7) the route woke on every PATCH carrying blockedByIssueIds: only when the set changed; (P8) comments read again from the margin were handed over twice: those the latest qualified runs carried are left out.

Writers of blocking relations and of done/cancelled statuses (by grep): direct wake through the one function for PATCH (blocker done, blocker set changed), the comment route's approval, DELETE of a blocker, the public MCP (it goes through PATCH), the native status decision and the decision cards (resolve_blocker, update_issue_status, cancel_issue_tree); the route's cancel keeps the STUDIO-0029 hand-back; every other writer is the backstop's (plugins, the runner's set_dependencies, recovery-action resolve, the watchdog fold, stalled review, interaction confirmation, onboarding move, quarantine restore, tree cancel, status cards, the escalation edge delete, company import). The backstop sees them by reading: recovery/work.ts loads assigned todo, in_progress and in_review issues in the stranded queue and blocked ones in the dependency queue, both call it before their own pass (heartbeat.ts); an empty blocker list reads as ready; only cancelled blockers left go through the hand-back comment; a changed assignee is covered by P4.

Each review defect, with its real-path case: non-assignee's run counted as handed over ("hands the comment to the Dev at the lift even after a non-assignee's run carried it"); cancelled plus open blocker, then the open one done ("hands the dependency back ... remaining blockers are all cancelled"); partial removal and deletion ("partial removal makes a todo/blocked issue ready", "its blocker issue is deleted"); only the last comment of a batch recorded ("holds at the claim gate the CTO comments merged in one queued run"); proof of the engine ("hands the comment over again after a run without a started engine, a run cut after its start, or a router refusal"); no signal ("notes once per series"); fixed wake key ("wakes once for each removal"); old traces ("ignores a hold trace older than the assignee's latest qualified run"); hand-over on every run ("adds nothing to the runs of an issue that was never blocked"); strict cancelled rule ("holds nothing once one unresolved blocker is cancelled"); claim exception moving the base ("marks a run passing the claim gate under an exception as bounded, with its admission as hand-over base"); cut between the hand-back comment and its wake ("wakes again a hand-back comment left without its wake"); two holds at once for the note ("writes one note when several agent comments are held at the same moment"); writers outside the function ("through one backstop pass after a direct service write", "after the runner's set_dependencies write", "wakes again on the next backstop pass when the hand-over run fails before the engine", and the mutant with the backstop removed); every edit of the set ("blocker list is emptied", "replaced by cancelled ones only"); a person's comment dropped by the wake merge ("keeps a person's comment written in the same PATCH as the blocker removal"); native decision and decision cards (five cases); swallowed failures and one failing wake ("still wakes the other dependents when the wake of one fails, and the backstop takes the lost one"); deduplication fooled by a skipped or failed wake ("wakes the hand-back comment again when its earlier wake failed, was skipped or was cancelled, not when it was delivered"); ready wake merged into a queued bounded run ("drops the bounded mode ..."), and into a running one ("still hands the held comment over when the blocker is done while a bounded run of the assignee is running"); agent-scoped trace ("sees a coalesced automatic hold as a trace after the base", "hands the held comment to a new assignee that a service write put on the issue, through the backstop"); issue.reassigned ("takes a case handoff's issue.reassigned activity as a reassignment trace"); unchanged blocker set ("sends no edit wake when a PATCH writes the same blocker set again").

Limits of these proofs: the plugin, set_dependencies and case-handoff cases make the same service writes as those callers, not the callers themselves; the failed, skipped and cancelled wake statuses of the hand-back case are set in the database; the logging of a failed wake is read in the code, not asserted.

Silences the backstop itself could create, and what prevents them: it stops only on a qualified run of the assignee after the trace (a queued wake only suspends it while alive); it cannot loop (doubling wait, 1 h at most, so a ticket whose runs never qualify is late, never silent); a cut between the hand-back comment and its wake, or after the wake, leaves the issue eligible; it does nothing while the assignee is not invocable or over budget, while a recovery action is active, or while scheduling is suppressed, and resumes after (each of these is visible elsewhere).

patches.origin: What: an agent's comment on a dependency-blocked issue does not start the assignee's run (admission and claim gate, one decision, agentCommentHeldByDependencies: only the assignee, only all-agent batches, never while any unresolved blocker is cancelled). A run that passes the claim gate under a dependency exception is marked dependencyBlockedInteraction; a dependency-resolved wake merged into a queued bounded run removes the mark. Handover (readCommentsToHandOver): the BASE of the current assignee on the issue is the time its latest qualified run was given its hand-over. A run qualifies when it succeeded with processStartedAt set and its admission computed a hand-over: it then carries heldDependencyHandoverAt, the admission time of that computation (a bounded run that carries the key computed and showed its batch, so it qualifies too: the hand-back on only cancelled blockers). A run WITHOUT the key never qualifies: a recovery run the server inserts with a fresh context (the immediate recovery after a release, the review participant's, provider_quota_recovery, the second disposition repair) passed no admission and was shown nothing, and so was a run of before this change (the first hand-over of an issue after the install reads the whole thread, the latest 20 named: one repeat per issue and assignee). The base is the admission, not the start, so a comment held after a queued run's admission stays after the base. A hand-over needs a trace since the base: a hold (the admission's skipped issue_dependencies_blocked request, read on requestedAt, updatedAt and finishedAt because a repeated automatic hold only moves updatedAt; or a run cancelled with that errorCode, at its cancellation time) that carries the mark of this change (heldDependencyTrace, HELD_DEPENDENCY_TRACE_KEY in run-dispatch/domain/wake-context.ts), of any agent since the current assignee's base (the issue may have been held for another assignee meanwhile and moved back by a writer that logs no activity; at worst a repeat); or an activity that reassigned the issue to it (issue.updated or issue.reassigned). The run that can act then carries every agent comment since the base, read from 10 s before it (HANDOVER_CLOCK_MARGIN_MS) and without the comments the latest qualified runs already carried (latest 20 named, the rest counted, heldDependencyReason for the packet text). A wake merged into a run that already started changes neither its bounded mark nor its hand-over. Every writer of a dependency hold sets the mark: the admission in the request payload (a repeated automatic hold also marks the earlier row it is merged into, execution-wait.ts), the claim gate, the retry gate and the stale native replacement cancel in the cancelled run's resultJson (run-dispatch/adapters/postgres.ts). The holds of before carry no mark and count for nothing: studio.21 held assignments and automatic wakes, never an agent's comment (it ran it bounded), so they hide nothing to hand over and the install wakes nobody. For a routed run processStartedAt means the command left for the worker machine (the router passes onSpawn through before the engine starts); succeeded is the real proof, and a run that succeeded without processStartedAt (its write is only logged on failure) does not qualify: at worst a repeat. One function, wakeDependentsAfterDependencyChange (dependency-change-wakes.ts), decides the dependents' wakes: ready dependents get issue_blockers_resolved, dependents left with only cancelled blockers are handed back (a system comment, woken again if its wake is missing, skipped, failed or cancelled), and a blocker cancelled outside the route gets the STUDIO-0029 hand-back. Its callers: the issue routes (PATCH blocker done, every blocker-set edit, the comment route's approval, DELETE of a blocker), the native status decision after commit (done and cancelled), and the decision cards after commit (resolve_blocker, update_issue_status, cancel_issue_tree), through the dependencies_changed post-commit action. After a native decision done the function sends no ready wake (readyAlreadyWoken): the decision's own transaction already woke every ready dependent, a dependent that is also the finished child's parent with issue_children_completed, which the ready-state lookup does not know; only the hand-back of the dependents left with cancelled blockers remains. Each dependent's wake is sent on its own: one that fails is logged and does not stop the others. The PATCH route calls the function only when the blocker set really changed. The route's addWakeup merges the comments of two wakes for the same agent and issue instead of dropping the first. The periodic hand-over backstop (recovery/held-comment-handover-backstop.ts) covers every other writer: plugins (setBlockedBy, issues.update), the runner tools (set_dependencies, update_status), recovery-action resolve, the watchdog fold, stalled review, interaction confirmation, onboarding move, quarantine restore, company import, a direct service write. It runs for each assigned open issue in the stranded-assignment and resolved-dependency recovery queues (recovery/work.ts:33, rebuilt every 30 s and on every notifyIssueRecovery): an issue with a hold trace after its assignee's base, ready or waiting only on cancelled blockers, with no live wake or run of the assignee, no active recovery action and an invocable assignee within budget, is woken (after the hand-back comment when only cancelled blockers are left). It stops when a qualified run moves the base past the trace; a run that fails, never reaches the engine, or was inserted without an admission leaves the issue eligible (the backstop waits for it while it is alive, then wakes). Never a loop: the first re-wake comes at the next pass, then the wait between two backstop wakes of one issue doubles (30 s, 1 min, 2 min, up to 1 h), counted from the backstop's own attempt rows since the base (a skipped request with the reason held_comment_handover_backstop_attempt, written before each wake, so the wait holds when the admission returns without writing a request or throws; read over 24 h at most); an issue whose runs never qualify (a router that refuses for hours, a run that succeeds without a recorded process start) is retried at most hourly, forever. Maximum delay for a forgotten writer: one rebuild (30 s) plus the pass; nothing while scheduling is suppressed, a recovery action is active or the assignee is not invocable, and it resumes after. No age bound on the traces; measured cost of one pass for one issue with 10,000 old skipped requests and 5,000 old runs of the assignee: median 4.0 to 5.0 ms, worst 12.6 to 14.4 ms over two runs (embedded PostgreSQL, WSL). issueService.update itself does not call the function (moved to the next batch, B20). A system note per assignee and per series says that a comment waits (signal only, under a lock on the issue). Why: TR-1258 (15 Nov 2026) and five independent reviews. Origin: studio fork only; to re-apply, keep held-dependency-comments.ts, held-dependency-notice.ts, dependency-change-wakes.ts and recovery/held-comment-handover-backstop.ts, their calls in queue.ts (claim gate with the exception marking, admission gate, handover), heartbeat.ts (the backstop in the stranded and dependencies recovery owners), run-preparation.ts (the held-comment window and text, the bounded mode dropped on a ready merge), issues.ts (the dependencies_changed post-commit action and its executor), decisions.ts and status-decision-committer.ts (the action queued after commit), routes/issues.ts (the calls of wakeDependentsAfterDependencyChange and the merge in addWakeup), and the mark of a dependency hold (wake-context.ts, execution-wait.ts, the two cancels in run-dispatch/adapters/postgres.ts); run dependency-blocked-comment-wake.test.ts and heartbeat-dependency-scheduling.test.ts.

patches.title: The Claude adapter's login markers read only the run's own error surface, and a usage limit outranks them: a run that ends on a limit is never sealed as claude_auth_required and never marks the AI account
patches.problem: Production 17 Nov 2026, run 21529e7e of a claude_local role (Dev Unity): the run ended on the weekly limit (resultJson: api_error_status 429, is_error true, subtype success, terminal_reason api_error, result "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6am"), but its error code was claude_auth_required. The login-prompt pattern (parse.ts, CLAUDE_LOGIN_PROMPT_RE) contains the bare word 'unauthorized' and was tried on every line of stdout; the run's transcript held 'But was: <System.UnauthorizedAccessException>', the output of a Unity test in a tool result. requiresLogin then outranked the quota classifier (execute.ts). The end of the run (run-lifecycle.ts, classifyAndPersistRunLiveness -> connection-intents.ts requestForRunAuthFailure -> ai-connections.ts markAuthenticationFailed) put the grant in needs_reauthorization and the connection in health error: the role stayed in error until its owner signed in again.

patches.origin: What: detectClaudeLoginRequired (parse.ts) reads the login-prompt markers only on the run's own error surface: the terminal fields of a FAILED result event (result, error, api_error, the errors list; never the result of a success or of a max-turns stop, which is the model's answer), the stdout lines that are not JSON events (a CLI that refuses to start writes 'Not logged in · Please run /login' as plain text), and stderr. It never reads the content of a tool_result nor the text of an assistant or user message. When the stream has no result event (it was cut), the CLI's own event-level error field (authentication_failed on an assistant or system event) is read, never a message. The capture keeps the last 4 MiB of stdout (MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES), so its first line can be the cut tail of an event: when the capture reached the cap, that first line is not read as plain text (a gap of upstream #13647). A terminal result that reports a usage limit (status 429, an api_error of usage or rate limit, or a quota phrase in the terminal fields of a failed result) outranks every login marker: the run is a limit (provider_quota and its usual wait, or a transient retry), never claude_auth_required. A 401 status on a failed terminal result is a login failure. The login URL keeps its broad scope. Server guard (ai-auth-failure.ts runResultReportsProviderLimit, used by connection-intents.ts requestForRunAuthFailure): a failed run whose own result reports a provider limit (status 429, an api_error of limit, errorFamily provider_quota) never marks the account and never asks for a new sign-in, whatever its error code; points 1 and 2 already make claude_auth_required a proof of a refused sign-in, the guard covers a Claude run stored earlier with the wrong code. It does NOT cover Codex as written here: a Codex result carries only stdout, stderr and the error family, which the login class overwrites; STUDIO-0065 adds a structured limit mark for it. Why: production 17 Nov 2026, run 21529e7e (see problem). patches.title: The Codex adapter's login-loss and limit classifiers read only the run's own error surface, recognise Codex's own login-loss sentences, and a usage limit outranks a login loss: a failed run whose transcript quotes an auth error never marks the shared OpenAI account, and a real login loss still does
patches.problem: The same defect as STUDIO-0064, found on 17 Nov 2026 by reading the code after the Claude incident. classifyCodexAuthRefreshFailure (codex-local parse.ts) tried its patterns on buildCodexErrorHaystack: the error message, the WHOLE stdout and stderr. The stdout of `codex exec --json` holds the output of every command the agent ran (command_execution) and the model's text (agent_message). The patterns include a contextual one: a word among oauth, refresh, access token, bearer, credential within 80 characters of 401, unauthorized or invalid grant. On a failed run (non-zero exit) a transcript line such as 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized ... bearer token' gave refresh_token_invalidated, evaluated BEFORE the usage limit (execute.ts). The refresh_token_* codes are authentication failures (ai-auth-failure.ts), so the end of the run marked the account as needing a new sign-in. Nearly every role of the studio runs on Codex and shares one OpenAI account: one such run would put all of them in error until the owner signs in again. The ACP lane had the same defect: it matched the patterns on the run's summary, the model's last text (acp.ts, withCodexAuthRefreshFailureClassification). Second defect, found by the independent review of the first version of this patch: the baseline's patterns do not recognise the sentences Codex really writes on a login loss (only 'refresh token has expired' matched); on the baseline a real loss was caught only through the trace Codex writes on stderr ('Failed to refresh token status=401 Unauthorized'). Reading stderr no longer once the protocol started, without patterns for the real sentences, would have left a real login loss unseen at every wake.

patches.origin: What. (1) Error surface: buildCodexErrorHaystack (parse.ts) reads the run's own error surface, through codexStdoutErrorSurface(stdout). Once the protocol started (an event of the Codex protocol was seen: thread.*, turn.*, item.*, error; another JSON object, a wrapper's, is a plain line and does not start it), only the LAST protocol error of the CURRENT turn counts (an `error` event or `turn.failed`; a recovered earlier error does not; turn.started and turn.completed forget the errors before them, so a non-zero exit after a turn that completed does not classify an old error): stderr, the plain stdout lines and the fallback error message built from stderr are not read, because stderr also carries the words of MCP servers, hooks and the ssh client of a routed run ('401 Unauthorized', an OAuth prompt), which are not about the AI account. That choice stays valid because Codex reports a login loss through the protocol too (the `error` event and `turn.failed` carry its sentence). When the protocol never started, the CLI failed before its stream: the error message the caller passes, the plain stdout lines and stderr are its own words and are read. The content of an item is never read: neither the output of a command or a tool, nor the model's text. The capture keeps the tail of stdout (runChildProcess, adapter-utils server-utils.ts:4783, appendWithCap at :4970, the last MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES = 4 MiB in CHARACTERS; appendWithByteCap is used only for the run-log excerpt, heartbeat/run-log.ts:15): when the capture reached the cap, its first line (the cut tail of an event) is not read as plain text; the comparison is made in bytes, which covers both helpers. (2) Codex's own sentences. Read in installed binaries, read only: codex-cli 0.166.0 (Linux x64, read on the worker machine WIN-02, sha256 b8a11fed..., by the worker router's chat) and codex-cli 0.156.1 (the npm Codex of the Paperclip server, installed with studio.21). Which Codex runs the roles (read in the database by the server pilot, read only, 17 Nov 2026): the non-routed Codex roles run on the roles server through ssh environments PK-OVH-<role>, with the command /srv/paperclip-<role>/bin/codex, in Codex 0.166.0 according to the infra record; Feedback Manager runs on QA-C through ssh with the command `codex`, version not read; Game Tester is routed to the worker machines, in 0.166.0. The npm Codex of the Paperclip server (0.156.1 and 0.160.0) serves no role run, except through the ACP lane, which no role uses. The sentences are therefore verified in the version that counts, 0.166.0 Linux x64, and in 0.156.1 too. Not verified: the exact binary of the roles server, the version on QA-C, and the macOS binary. The same texts in both versions read:'Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used. Please log out and sign in again.' -> refresh_token_reused; '... because your refresh token has expired. ...' -> refresh_token_expired; '... because your refresh token was revoked. ...', '... because you have since logged out or signed in to another account. Please sign in again.', 'Your access token could not be refreshed. Please log out and sign in again.' and 'Your authentication session could not be refreshed automatically. Please log out and sign in again.' -> refresh_token_invalidated. The specific sentences are tried first. The binaries hold no refresh_token_reused, refresh_token_expired or refresh_token_invalidated code as text: the code patterns of the baseline are kept, and they are no proof of a real form. The stderr trace 'ERROR codex_login::auth::manager: Failed to refresh token status=401 Unauthorized' is read only when the protocol never started. 'Failed to refresh token: <cause>' alone is not a class (the cause can be the network). 'ChatGPT login is required, but an API key is currently being used. Logging out.' is not a class (not a login loss of the account). (3) MCP: in the binaries invalid_grant appears only in MCP OAuth texts ('The MCP authorization server rejected the enterprise grant: invalid_grant'). The generic patterns (invalid_grant, an auth word near 401 or unauthorized) are not tried on a line that names MCP, wherever Codex writes it; Codex's own sentences still are. (4) One surface for the login-loss, usage-limit, transient and retry-time classifiers: the limit now outranks the login loss, so a transcript that quotes 'usage limit' must not be able to hide a real login loss. execute.ts evaluates the usage limit first and the login loss only without a limit, and writes providerLimitObserved: true in the result when it classified a limit. (5) acp.ts (the ACP lane) no longer matches the patterns on result.summary, the model's last text, and leaves a run already classified as provider_quota alone. (6) Server guard (ai-auth-failure.ts, runResultReportsProviderLimit, introduced by STUDIO-0064): it reads structured fields only, never the run's output; a Codex result carries no status, so the guard reads the adapter's providerLimitObserved mark, and honours it for a codex_local run only (connection-intents.ts reads the adapter type of the run's agent). A Codex run stored before this change with a login code and a limit in its output carries no mark and is not caught if it is processed again. codex-local/src/server/index.ts is not changed (the router pins its built file). This patch is stacked on STUDIO-0064: it extends the same guard function, and it corrects the STUDIO-0064 record, which said that its guard covered the other adapters. Why: see problem. Engine in use (read in the database by the server pilot, 17 Nov 2026): the 18 codex_local agents of the studio all run the CLI engine, none the ACP engine. The ACP lane is corrected with a unit case only. Not changed, to look at in B20: 'Not logged in. Please run `codex login`' in a run's output is not a login-loss class on the baseline (no pattern of parse.ts reads it; only the environment test does) and does not become one; a bare 401 without an auth word is not one either. On the ACP lane classifyCodexTerminalSessionFailure (acp.ts) still gives acpx_auth_required for '401 unauthorized' in the title and details of a terminal failure: not changed, no role uses ACP. gemini_local (gemini-local parse.ts:285-299) and kimi_local (kimi-local parse.ts:228-236) have the same whole-output defect; the studio does not use them, they are not changed. Live steering (experimentalLiveSteering). The adapter itself never starts an app-server for a run: without a codexPreparedProcess hook it runs `codex exec --json` whatever the toggle (execute.ts, the prepared-process branch). The hook is supplied by the worker router's wrapper, for routed runs and, through its direct executor, for non-routed agents whose toggle is on. The adapter then receives a stdout COMPOSED by the router in the `codex exec` format (thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed or turn.failed) and an empty stderr. Router 0.30.x composes turn.failed with a fixed text ('Interactive provider turn did not complete successfully.') and ignores the app-server's error notifications: on that path a login loss is seen neither on the baseline nor here (not a regression; a test shows it). The correction belongs to the router (carry the app-server's message into turn.failed); once it does, this patch classifies it (a test with a composed turn.failed that carries Codex's sentence, without stderr). The detection on that path therefore depends on the message the router transmits. The non-routed roles run through ssh too, so with the toggle on they take the router's direct executor and the same composed stdout (read in a local tree of the router at 4f18ca7: runtime.js:254, direct-interactive.js:7-18, interactive.js:104 and :201). What the adapter sees there on a login loss: if the app-server ends the turn as failed, a turn.failed with the fixed text, an empty stderr and exit code 1 (no class, no error code, the account is not marked); if the app-server refuses a request (initialize, thread/start, turn/start) or asks the client for something (an auth request is answered with an error, router_interactive_client_request_unsupported), the hook throws and the adapter classifies nothing at all. The app-server's `error` notification is not handled by the router. The same on the baseline. Origin: adapted from paperclipai/paperclip#15832 (head 10be54bcba); stderr and the plain stdout lines once the protocol started are not read here (upstream keeps stderr after the protocol started); Codex's own sentences, the turn reset, the protocol event types, the MCP lines, the capped-capture guard, the shared surface for the limit classifiers, the limit-first order, the ACP lane and the structured mark for the server guard are studio additions. patches.problem: Production, 17 Nov 2026, TR-1526. At 16:01:15 the Unity developer handed the task to the CTO in review, by a change of assignee alone; its run 84d24f1c was cancelled with issue_reassigned. At 16:01:18 the CTO's issue_assigned wake met getExecutionBlocker: the stopped run's process was still alive (conversation-continuation.ts, getConversationOwnershipBlocker) and its environment lease was released at 16:01:32 only: execution_owner_active, recoveryActionId null. In heartbeat/queue.ts, deferBlockedExecution kept a blocked wake as deferred_issue_execution only for a durable request, a comment, a card context or a native intent; any other wake went to recordExecutionWait, which writes a skipped receipt that nothing reads again. The CTO had no run until a comment 58 minutes later. Measured since 15 Nov (read only, by the server pilot): nine such wakes; four were saved within 16 to 24 s by another wake, three stayed without a run (TR-1188 33 min, TR-1331 30 min, TR-1526 58 min). The role sheets published on 17 Nov make a role return its machine and hand the task over in the same run, so the hand-over nearly always falls while the process stops.

A run of the Unity developer is started by the heartbeat; its stand-in adapter starts a real child process, reports it as the run's process (onSpawn, with the start time read from the system) and returns only when the run is stopped. A sweep starts nothing while the child lives. Once the child is stopped, the stopped run still holds through a reconciliation action (the stand-in adapter returns no stop receipt): the kept wake waits; past ten minutes one system note tells the thread what holds (the action's own next action), once, and nothing starts. When that action is cancelled, a sweep retires the kept copy and the CTO gets exactly one run, whose context carries neither the wait nor the mark; another sweep starts nothing. (b) The same behind a stopped run's process and behind its environment lease (seeded rows, as in STUDIO-0041). (c) A second and a third hand-over wake are counted on the kept one (coalescedCount 2, updatedAt unchanged, no skipped receipt), and one run starts. The kept copy is then retired as skipped and re-admitted through ordinary admission, which applies every gate again. (3) Bounded exit (execution-owner-stall-notice.ts). When a hold still keeps the wake waiting ten minutes after it was asked for, the sweep writes one system note in the thread, once per hold (a marker carries the run id and, for a recovery action, its id; under a lock on the issue row). The wake stays kept and starts as soon as the hold is gone. The note wakes nobody. (4) Release drain (wake-queue use-cases.ts, runReleaseDrain). A kept hand-over wake carries nothing a run must read. When the run that releases the task is the same agent's, on this task, and succeeded, it served the hand-over: the kept copy is cancelled with that reason instead of being promoted into a second run (four of the nine production cases were served within seconds by another wake). If the task is handed on again before the owner lets go, the first assignee's kept wake is no longer re-admitted by the sweep, and the drain, which reads the oldest deferred wake of the task whatever its agent, would promote it at the next release: a former assignee would run on a task that is no longer its own. Two rules retire it: the drain cancels a kept hand-over wake whose agent is not the task's assignee, and admission, when it keeps a wake for the current assignee, cancels the kept hand-over wakes of the other agents on the task. Still lost: a wake of an agent that is not the assignee, without a comment or a card, behind the previous owner. Noted by the independent review, not changed. The scope is wider than a hand-over: any wake of the current assignee without a comment or a card is kept behind the hold, also behind its own dying run; a later wake of another reason is counted on the first one and its reason is lost. 'Served by' exists for a succeeded run only: if the new assignee's run fails, the kept wake is promoted into another run, which can add to the retry of the failure. A kept wake whose task turns done or cancelled stays deferred.
